## Goal
Remove the now-unused `'onImpact'` AOE projectile-detonation machinery (dead code retained by AH-0MUUF9GZV004WVT9) and its tests, now that no catalogue weapon uses the `'onImpact'` trigger.

## Context
AH-0MUUF9GZV004WVT9 moved the Mortar from `'onImpact'` to `'onRandom'`, so the `'onImpact'` path is no longer referenced by any weapon definition. Per project dead-code discipline it was deliberately retained during that change; this item is the follow-up cleanup (discovered-from:AH-0MUUF9GZV004WVT9).

## Scope (in)
- `src/utils/weapons.ts`: drop `'onImpact'` from the `AoETrigger` union; remove the `onImpact` descriptor doc; remove `AOE_PROJECTILE_SPEEDS` if it has no remaining consumer (the Mortar's range basis is to be made explicit separately if needed).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`: remove the `onAoeProjectileSpawned` hook and the `'onImpact'` branch in `_autoFire` (bullet spawn is then only unreachable; decide whether projectile spawn remains for any weapon).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`: remove `onAoeProjectileSpawned`, `detonateAoeProjectile`, the `bullet.aoeWeapon` handling in `onPlayerBulletHitsEnemy`, and the mortar VFX/sound path from `spawnAoeDetonationVfx` if unused.
- `src/entities/PlayerBullet.ts`: remove `aoeWeapon`, `aoeDetonated`, `onExpire` (if only used by the AOE path) and their comments.
- `src/scenes/core/AoeWeapons.test.ts`: remove the retained `onImpact` tests (the section marked 'Retained onImpact projectile-detonation machinery (dead code)').
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`: remove `onAoeProjectileSpawned`/`detonateAoeProjectile` from `SHARED_AOE_METHODS`.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`: update the descriptor union text (remove `'onImpact'`) and any remaining onImpact references.

## Out of scope
- Any behavioural change to Nova, Mortar or Arc.
- Removing the generic player-bullet spawn path used by conventional weapons.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1 — `AoETrigger` is `'onFire' | 'onRandom'`; no source references `'onImpact'` remain (except historical docs/changelog if intentionally kept — enumerate any).
- [ ] AC2 — The onImpact hooks/methods and `PlayerBullet` AOE fields are removed, and `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean.
- [ ] AC3 — The retained-onImpact tests are removed; `AoeWeapons.test.ts` still covers Nova/Arc/Mortar random detonation.
- [ ] AC4 — Gym↔game parity guard (`CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) still passes with the reduced `SHARED_AOE_METHODS`.
- [ ] AC5 — Docs (`docs/Game Design Document.md`) still pass `src/aoeDocs.test.ts` (or are updated if the guard references removed strings).
- [ ] AC6 — Full suite green (`/skill:test`).

## Notes / risks
- `spawnAoeDetonationVfx` (Mortar burst + cue, off-screen culling) is still needed by the `'onRandom'` path — do not remove it.
- The generic `spawnPlayerBullet` path must remain for the cannon/spread/dual/rapid.
- If any consumer of `AOE_PROJECTILE_SPEEDS` remains as the Mortar range basis, either keep it (renamed/documented) or replace the range basis explicitly; do not silently drop the Mortar range.
data.title: Remove the onImpact projectile-detonation machinery and its tests

# Halve bulletSpeed in unknown-archetype fallbacks

## Problem statement

AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ halves the enemy `bulletSpeed` of the eight shipped archetypes
across the runtime CSV, `DEFAULT_ENEMY_CONFIGS` and the per-entity constants.
During planning, three additional runtime fallbacks were found that also hard-code
`bulletSpeed: 200` for **unknown** archetype keys and were explicitly out of that
item's scope (its Q2 enumeration covered only CSV + defaults + entity constants):

- `src/core/configStore.ts` — `genericEnemyDefault()`
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — `resolveBaseConfig()`
- `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts` — `groupEnemyConfig()`

Leaving them at 200 means an unknown-key enemy would fire at double the speed of
every shipped archetype, so tuning can still drift for that edge case.

## Desired change

Decide and, if accepted, halve these three `bulletSpeed` fallbacks (200 → 100) for
consistency, updating any affected difficulty-sequencer expectations.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — The three unknown-archetype fallbacks use `bulletSpeed: 100` (or a
  documented decision is recorded to leave them at 200 with rationale).
- [ ] AC2 — Any difficulty-sequencer or difficulty-scoring test affected by the
  change is updated and the full suite passes.
- [ ] AC3 — The decision and rationale are recorded on this item.

## Key Files

- `src/core/configStore.ts`
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts`
- `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts`

## Related work

- AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ — Reduce bullet speed of enemies (parent discovery; strictly out of its scope).
data.title: Halve bulletSpeed in unknown-archetype fallbacks

discovered-from:AH-0MUYRJQE50021T4A

## Problem

Several deterministic bot micro-simulations are knife-edge calibrations: a subtle, legitimate gameplay tweak (e.g. the 1-5% gentler thrust-press reduction in AH-0MUYRJQE50021T4A) flips their outcomes because scores are dominated by discrete hit/bullet collisions.

During AH-0MUYRJQE50021T4A two tests had to be recalibrated:
- src/ai/style/evaluation.test.ts - synthetic human seed moved 7 -> 14.
- src/ai/framework/competent/competentBot.integration.test.ts - RUN_SEED moved 0x0b07 -> 0x0b16.

On the base behaviour, src/ai/style/evaluation.test.ts already regressed on 13/24 seeds, and the competent-vs-legacy AC6 test only wins in base because the legacy bot chaotically collides with bullets; without bullets the legacy bot scored higher (22 vs 20) on base.

## Goal

Make these tests robust rather than seed-picked:
- Aggregate competence/style comparisons over a set of seeds (e.g. assert the styled/competent bot is not systematically worse), or
- Compare on scenarios whose score is not dominated by discrete collisions.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: The style-match AC4 demonstration no longer depends on a single lucky seed (e.g. asserts over multiple seeds).
- AC2: The competent-vs-legacy AC6 test asserts an objective-based advantage rather than relying on chaotic bullet collisions.
- AC3: Recalibrating either test is not required by an unrelated small bot-feel tweak.
- AC4: Full test suite, typecheck and build pass.
data.title: Make bot micro-simulation tests robust to small feel tweaks

## Goal

De-risk the arena's campaign integration (AH-0MV8QT7CB0060A7A) before any build work: prove the shared campaign and upgrade-choice systems can run headless under Node/vitest with the same seed derivation the game uses, and identify every impure dependency so the design uses the shared core directly or a named thin adapter — never a divergent copy.

## Headline

A short spike that instantiates/runs the modules the arena will consume — `buildSequencedLevels` (src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts, all fixed/curve/dynamic modes), `sequencer`/`defaultCandidatePool` (src/core/difficultySequencer.ts), `WaveManager` (src/waves/WaveManager.ts), `chooseOptions`/`buildChoiceCandidates` (src/powerups/choice.ts), `MineralHold` (src/core/GameState.ts hold), and the hold-full reward application path (`applyMineralChoiceReward`, src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts) — and records exactly which are headless-pure and which need an adapter (e.g. the `EffectsRegistry` the reward applyer requires).

## Context

- The eval layer (src/ai/eval/) must stay pure: no wall clock, no I/O, no Phaser import.
- Gym↔game parity (AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1): an enabled behaviour runs the same code in gym/game and in the eval arena.
- Effort-and-risk unknowns recorded on the parent: can `sequencedLevels.ts` run headless without Phaser imports? Can the reward-application path be exercised without a Phaser `EffectsRegistry`?

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1:** A vitest smoke test imports and exercises each target module without importing Phaser or a wall-clock/IO module in the eval entry path; the smoke test lives under src/ai/eval/ (e.g. a `campaignHeadless.test.ts` spike scaffold).
- **AC2:** Every impure dependency found is listed with a concrete adapter plan (thin, named, headless) or a recommendation to not model that behaviour in this item — recorded in a comment on this work item.
- **AC3:** The spike records the design decision the arena build follows: consume each shared entry point directly vs via the named adapter, with the seed derivation (createSeededRng + buildSequencedLevels {seed}) confirmed to be deterministic.
- **AC4:** The spike makes no production code changes outside src/ai/eval/ evaluation-only scaffolding; the finding is reproducible by a maintainer (commands recorded).

## Key Files

**Key Files:**
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — campaign builder (fixed/curve/dynamic modes) to prove headless-safe
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — sequencer + candidate pool to prove headless-safe
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — wave/level state machine to prove headless-safe
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — shared upgrade-choice flow to prove headless-safe
- `src/core/GameState.ts` — MineralHold (capacity/growth/overflow)
- `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts` — applyMineralChoiceReward (EffectsRegistry dependency to assess)
- `src/ai/eval/campaignHeadless.test.ts` (new vitest spike scaffold) — headless-import smoke coverage
data.title: Spike: prove the shared campaign core runs headless (wave sequencer + upgrade choices)

## Goal

Replace the arena's fixed two-to-N-wave hostile reservoir (skirmish model) with the **shared campaign sequencer**: the arena builds the shipped campaign via `buildSequencedLevels(rows, defaultCandidatePool, { seed })` (honouring `fixed`/`curve`/`dynamic` generation modes), drives the shared `WaveManager` state machine, spawns from `planSpawns(seededRng)`, gates wave/level completion through `onEnemyDestroyed`, and emits the canonical `wave_start`/`wave_cleared`/`level_cleared` telemetry events so `waveReached` and `levelReached` become meaningful, non-zero distributions in batch reports.

## User story

As a game designer, I want a bot batch to play the same campaign the game ships (all levels/waves via the shared sequencer), so per-wave difficulty targets can be tuned from evidence instead of intuition.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1:** One arena run plays the shared campaign (all levels and waves of the shipped definition, including `fixed`/`curve`/`dynamic` generation modes) and emits real `wave_start`/`wave_cleared`/`level_cleared` records with the canonical payloads from `runTelemetry.ts` (`level`, `waveNumber`, `waveCount`); a batch report shows non-zero `waveReached`/`levelReached`.
- **AC2:** Wave/level progression is driven exclusively by the shared `WaveManager` (`beginGame`, `planSpawns`, `onEnemyDestroyed`) and `buildSequencedLevels` — no divergent copy of campaign, wave, enemy or ship stats in src/ai/eval/ (asserted by the existing duplicate-body/parity guards).
- **AC3:** The `dynamic` wave mode derives from the run seed exactly as the game does (buildSequencedLevels `{ seed }`), so two runs with the same seed produce the same campaign for byte-identical telemetry.
- **AC4:** The Level-10 boss trigger is treated as the end of the run (no boss/mini-boss simulation this round — fidelity boundary, parent Q2=a); the boundary is documented in code.
- **AC5:** Determinism preserved: same seed + config + policy produces identical records on the campaign path; run never reads the wall clock.
- **AC6:** Unit tests cover progression, canonical event emission, seed-derived dynamic mode, and the no-divergent-copy guard; they pass under Node/vitest headless.

## Key Files

**Key Files:**
- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` — drive buildSequencedLevels + WaveManager; emit wave/level events
- `src/ai/eval/arena.test.ts` — campaign progression, event payloads, dynamic-mode seed tests
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — shared state machine consumed by the arena
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — shared campaign builder (fixed/curve/dynamic)
- `src/waves/Formations.ts` — static LEVELS skeleton merged by the builder
- `src/scenes/core/runTelemetry.ts` — canonical wave_start/wave_cleared/level_cleared event names
- `src/ai/eval/types.ts` — telemetry/types consumed by metrics (verify/keep)
data.title: Arena plays the shipped campaign through the shared WaveManager

## Goal

Model the mineral hold and the hold-full upgrade-choice loop in the arena using the **shared choice system** (`chooseOptions`/`randomChoiceStrategy` from src/powerups/choice.ts with the run's seeded RNG), so the arena emits `hold_full` and canonical `choice_selected` events and report `upgradesSelected` becomes a meaningful per-choice-id distribution. The bot picks among the offered options using the same seeded stream (parent Q1=a). Choices permanently affect the run (ownership context carried into later choice offers) via the headless-safe adapter identified in the spike child.

## User story

As the automated-balancing maintainer, I want the arena to exercise the same upgrade-choice flow the game ships, so per-upgrade balance can be measured from bot runs.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1:** A run collects minerals into a shared-model hold (`MineralHold` semantics: capacity, growth multiplier, overflow); when the hold fills, the arena offers options via shared `chooseOptions(3, randomChoiceStrategy, seededRng, context)` and emits `hold_full` with the offered option ids.
- **AC2:** The bot selects one offered option via the run's seeded RNG stream; the arena emits `choice_selected` with the canonical `{ index, id }` payload; a batch report shows non-zero per-choice-id `upgradesSelected` distributions.
- **AC3:** The reward is applied through the shared reward path (or the named headless adapter from the spike) so later choice offers carry accurate owned-weapon/power-up context (weapon-level/power-up-level options) — no invented option model in src/ai/eval/.
- **AC4:** Deterministic per seed: the same seed yields the same choice offers and selections (byte-identical telemetry).
- **AC5:** Unit tests cover hold-full triggering, canonical event payloads, ownership-context carry-over, and seeded determinism; they pass headless under Node/vitest.

## Key Files

**Key Files:**
- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` — mineral hold, choice offers, selection, choice_selected emission
- `src/ai/eval/arena.test.ts` — hold-full, event payloads, ownership context, determinism tests
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — shared chooseOptions/randomChoiceStrategy/buildChoiceCandidates
- `src/core/GameState.ts` — MineralHold semantics (capacity, growth, overflow)
- `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts` — applyMineralChoiceReward (headless adapter from spike)
- `src/scenes/core/runTelemetry.ts` — canonical hold_full/choice_selected event names
- `src/ai/eval/metrics.ts` — already parses choice_selected; verify/keep
- **AC6 (parent-AC2 traceability):** The bot makes upgrade selections through the shared upgrade-choice flow and `choice_selected` events are emitted; a batch report shows non-zero per-choice-id `upgradesSelected` distributions.
data.title: Arena resolves hold-full upgrade choices through the shared choice flow

## Goal

Make the full-campaign arena path the default in batch mode (parent Q3=b) and expose the config/CLI surface: `ArenaConfig`/`BatchConfig` gain a `campaign` surface defaulting to **true**, `scripts/evaluate.mjs` gains a `--skirmish` flag (and keeps `--batch`/`--games`/`--policies`/`--ticks`), a full-campaign run is bounded by a finite tick budget (higher default than the current 1800; `gameComplete`/death ends the run early), and the balance report's existing per-wave/per-level aggregation consumes the new events unchanged.

## User story

As the automated-balancing maintainer, I want `--batch` to automatically exercise the full shipped campaign, so the default report reflects what players experience without extra flags.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1:** `--batch` and `--games N` with no extra flags play full campaigns and the report shows non-zero `waveReached`/`levelReached`/`upgradesSelected` distributions.
- **AC2:** `--skirmish` opts back into the previous single-level skirmish path (backward compatible for existing consumers/tests).
- **AC3:** Campaign runs are finitely bounded — a configurable tick budget with a sane higher default, early exit on death or `gameComplete` (boss trigger); no unbounded simulation.
- **AC4:** Batch determinism preserved: same seeds + config + policies produce a byte-identical serialised balance report (`recordsHash` stable).
- **AC5:** Single-run evaluation (`runEvaluation`, A/B, human comparison) keeps the skirmish semantics and the difference is documented (report comparability note) — changed only by deliberate later work.
- **AC6:** CLI/engine/report unit tests cover the new defaults and both modes.

## Key Files

**Key Files:**
- `src/ai/eval/types.ts` — ArenaConfig/BatchConfig campaign surface (default true)
- `src/ai/eval/engine.ts` — runBatch campaign default + bounded tick budget
- `src/ai/eval/cli.ts` — --skirmish flag parsing, campaign surface in runConfig
- `scripts/evaluate.mjs` — shell flag wiring (--skirmish, default campaign)
- `src/ai/eval/engine.test.ts` — batch default/campaign/skirmish tests
- `src/ai/eval/cli.test.ts` — CLI flag tests
- `src/ai/eval/report.ts` — per-wave/per-level aggregation (verify unchanged)
data.title: Full-campaign batch runs by default with a bounded tick budget

## Goal

Verify the campaign arena path's three hard guarantees with acceptance tests, so the balance loop (AH-0MV8Q5EYE001R715) can trust the richer reports: byte-identical replay, config sensitivity (a `difficulty-curves.csv` edit or upgrade-definition edit measurably shifts the corresponding distributions for the same seeds), and no wall-clock/IO in the pure eval core (parent AC4/AC5/AC7).

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1:** A test replays the same seed + config + policy on the campaign path twice and asserts byte-identical records / stable `recordsHash`.
- **AC2:** A test edits a difficulty-curve row (e.g. raises a wave's `targetDifficulty`) and asserts the same seeds produce a measurably different `waveReached`/`levelReached` distribution.
- **AC3:** A test edits an upgrade definition and asserts the same seeds produce a measurably different `upgradesSelected` distribution.
- **AC4:** A guard test asserts the pure eval core (arena/metrics/engine) never imports a wall-clock or I/O module on its campaign path; campaign progression, upgrade-choice emission, single-source-of-truth, config sensitivity and determinism are all covered by unit tests (parent AC7 umbrella).
- **AC5:** All new tests pass headless under Node/vitest and run in the full suite.

## Key Files

**Key Files:**
- `src/ai/eval/arena.test.ts` — byte-identical replay + no-wall-clock guard tests
- `src/ai/eval/engine.test.ts` — recordsHash stability and config-sensitivity batch tests
- `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` — edit target difficulty for sensitivity test
- `src/powerups/types.ts` — POWER_UP_CATALOGUE (edit an upgrade definition for sensitivity test)
- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — weapon tuning (alternative upgrade-definition edit target)
- **AC6 (parent-AC4 traceability):** Same seed + config + policy ⇒ byte-identical campaign report; `recordsHash` stable; no wall-clock/IO in the pure eval core.
- **AC7 (parent-AC5 traceability):** Editing `difficulty-curves.csv` (e.g. raising a wave’s `targetDifficulty`) and/or an upgrade definition measurably changes the corresponding report distribution for the same seeds, verified by test.
data.title: Determinism and config-sensitivity acceptance tests for the campaign path

# Shared emergence-path wiring & gym↔game parity

Wire the new per-enemy shimmer and the wormhole glow/pulse ring through the shared spawn-animation path and the shared `wormholeEffects` lifecycle so the shipped game and every combat gym consume identical code (gym↔game parity convention, AGENTS.md). Minimal wiring only — all behaviour lives in the shared VFX helpers.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene` (+ its subclasses) drive the per-enemy shimmer and wormhole ring through the same shared helpers in the spawn-animation path — no divergent copies of the shimmer/ring behaviour.
- The wormhole glow/pulse ring lifecycle is wired into the existing `wormholeEffects` registry usage (`CombatScene.wormholeEffects`, cleared on `SHUTDOWN`).
- The repo-wide duplicate-body guard in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` and the gym-parity docs assertion pass unchanged.
- Minimal diff: the change touches only shared wiring call sites (`CombatScene`/`CombatCoreScene`/`PlayScene`/`GymFormationScene`) — no new behaviour copies.
- Full project test suite passes with the wiring in place.

## Problem

`implement.py parent` decides whether a child worktree contains work via `_git_path_has_changes()` (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`), whose docstring says it returns True when the worktree HEAD *differs* from the parent branch. A child worktree that is merely **behind** `dev` (HEAD != `dev`, but zero commits ahead and no dirty files) is therefore classified as "has changes" and `phase_parent` immediately runs `finish` on it.

Observed 2026-10-19 during the AH-0MVF3BESP005ZDAV epic:

1. `implement.py drive` started child AH-0MVF6XLBQ002GYWQ and its session was killed at the 3600 s timeout with a clean worktree (no edits, no commits).
2. While the drive was running, three unrelated commits landed on `dev`, so the child worktree was 3 commits behind.
3. `implement.py parent` reported `Child AH-0MVF6XLBQ002GYWQ has changes — running finish subprocess...` and ran `finish` on empty work. `finish`'s changed-scope selection was unavailable and fell back to a full-suite run (~10 min under load), which failed and reported `Failed to finish child`.

## Expected behaviour

A worktree with no dirty files and **no commits ahead of** the parent branch must be treated as "no work" (return the child as `next_child` for implementation), regardless of how far behind it is. The worktree placement guard should likewise not be affected.

## Suggested fix

- In `_git_path_has_changes()`, replace the "HEAD differs from parent branch" test with an ahead-count test (`git rev-list --count <parent>..HEAD` > 0) so behind-only worktrees are clean.
- Add a regression test covering: clean worktree at the fork base, clean worktree behind `dev`, dirty worktree, worktree with one commit ahead.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** A child worktree with no uncommitted changes and no commits ahead of the parent branch is not treated as having changes by `phase_parent` (covered by a unit test).
- **AC2:** A child worktree that is behind `dev` but has no local commits does not trigger a `finish` subprocess.
- **AC3:** Worktrees with commits ahead, or with dirty files, are still detected as having changes (no regression).
data.title: implement.py: behind-only child worktree mis-detected as 'has changes' and auto-finished

# Pure scene-capture module: config parsing, validation and timing

The pure, browser-free core of the multi-scene capture feature (AH-0MUX2NLFZ00128WC): parses and validates the scene-list JSON config, derives the watchable gym scene set, builds the per-scene capture plan (including the two 0.25 s fades), and formats the `--json` payload. No server, browser or Playwright imports — fully hermetic and unit-tested, consumed by the capture driver (sibling item). A shared browser-free registry of watchable gym scene keys mirrors the existing `CAPTURE_SCENARIOS` parity pattern (`scripts/capture-scenarios.mjs`) so the CLI pre-boot validation and the page-side director agree on the same set.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Covers parent AC1.** A JSON config file specifies an ordered, arbitrary-length list of scenes; each entry carries a `target` (gym scene key), a `playMs` duration, a `captureMs` duration, and an optional `label`. The file is parsed and validated **before** any server/browser boots, failing fast with an actionable, non-zero-exit error for a missing/unreadable/malformed file, an unknown or unsupported `target`, an empty scene list, or a non-positive/non-numeric `playMs`/`captureMs` (mirroring the existing `--count` validation style).
- **Watchable target set.** The watchable gym scene set is derived from the discovered gym scenes minus the parameterised `GymFodderEnemies` and `GymLevel`; unknown or unsupported targets are rejected.
- **Scene-plan builder.** A pure builder computes per-scene `{ target, playMs, captureMs, startMs, endMs }`, inserting the two 0.25 s fades (`SCENE_FADE_MS = 250`) between consecutive scenes; exported, side-effect-free, deterministic.
- **JSON payload builder.** A pure builder reports per-scene timings, the total output duration and the output path.
- **Tests green.** The test-first sibling suite (`Tests: scene-capture config, timing and director keys`) passes; `scripts/capture-scenes.d.mts` declares the exported types.

## Key Files

- `scripts/capture-scenes.mjs` (new)
- `scripts/capture-scenes.d.mts` (new)
- `scripts/capture-scenes.test.ts` (sibling test item)
- `scripts/capture-scenarios.mjs` (shared browser-free registry parity pattern)
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` (`parseCaptureCount` validation style reference)
- `src/utils/gymDiscovery.ts` (discovered gym scene key convention, `Gym<Name>`)

# Dev-gated in-page capture scene director

A dev-only page-side handle (`window.__aiHellCaptureDirector`) that switches the already-running page to a discovered gym scene by key, so one continuously-running `MediaRecorder` can span every scene of a multi-scene capture (AH-0MUX2NLFZ00128WC). Inert in production builds; mirrors the established `window.__aiHellScenario` dev-gated handle pattern (`src/core/devScenario.ts`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Covers parent AC2.** A dev-only page-side handle — e.g. `window.__aiHellCaptureDirector.start(key)` — starts a discovered, non-parameterised gym scene by key **inside the already-running page** (no navigation/reload), so one continuously-running `MediaRecorder` spans every scene. It is inert in production builds (`import.meta.env.DEV` gate; `npm run check-bundle` still passes) and rejects unknown/unsupported keys (including the parameterised `GymFodderEnemies` and `GymLevel`) with a clear error rather than silently doing nothing.
- **Key resolution pure.** A pure, unit-tested resolver accepts the discovered non-parameterised gym scene keys and rejects everything else.
- **Boot registration.** The handle is registered at boot (`src/core/boot.ts`) in dev builds only; unit tests cover both the key-validation logic and the dev gate.
- **No navigation.** Starting a scene neither navigates nor reloads the page; the game instance and the running recorder keep going.

## Key Files

- `src/core/captureDirector.ts` (new)
- `src/core/captureDirector.test.ts` (new)
- `src/core/devScenario.ts` (established dev-gated `window` handle pattern — mirror it)

2. `registerCaptureDirector(game)`: attach `window.__aiHellCaptureDirector = { start(key) { resolve…; game.scene.start(key); } }` gated by `import.meta.env.DEV`.
3. Register the call in `src/core/boot.ts` dev-only, mirroring the `devScenario` handle placement.

# Multi-scene capture driver: one recorder, fades, single WebM

The orchestrator slice of the multi-scene capture feature (AH-0MUX2NLFZ00128WC): boots one dev server + one browser, drives the in-page director and the page-side fade overlay, records every scene with a single `MediaRecorder`, and writes exactly one WebM plus the `--json` payload. Reuses the existing capture machinery (server boot, mime selection, audio tap, probe, progress) rather than duplicating it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Covers parent AC3.** A single `MediaRecorder` captures the scenes in config order; between consecutive scenes a page-side canvas overlay fades **to** black over 0.25 s then **from** black over 0.25 s before the next scene's play window, and the fade is present in the recorded video (the recorder captures the overlay). The scene count is arbitrary (verified with at least three scenes).
- **Covers parent AC4.** The command writes exactly **one** WebM (`video/webm;codecs=vp9,opus`, falling back per the existing `resolveCaptureMimeType` order) containing all scenes plus their transitions at 960×540 with the game's own SFX, and the result passes the existing non-trivial video+audio probe. The `--json` payload reports per-scene `{ target, playMs, captureMs, startMs, endMs }` timings and the total output duration/file path.
- **Entry point.** `npm run capture:scenes -- --config <file>` is the documented CLI entry point; the config is parsed and validated before any server or browser boots.
- **Reuse.** Reuses the existing pure capture machinery (Vite server boot, headless Chromium, mime selection, audio tap, probe, progress) rather than duplicating it.
- **Fade injection.** Playwright injects the fade overlay and calls the director between scenes; the recorder and page are never reloaded across the batch.

## Key Files

- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` (expose/reuse the server-boot, browser, recorder and probe plumbing, or add a `--scenes` mode)
- `scripts/capture-scenes.mjs` (sibling pure module — config/plan/payload)
- `scripts/capture-scenes.d.mts` / `scripts/capture-scenes.test.ts` (siblings)
- `src/core/captureDirector.ts` (sibling director for in-page scene switching)
- `package.json` (`capture:scenes` script)
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` (documented by the docs item)

## Minimal Implementation

1. Add a `--scenes <config>` mode (or a small sibling orchestrator) reusing the `runCaptureSession`-style server/browser boot and recorder/probe plumbing.
2. Before any boot: parse + validate the config via the pure module; map validation errors to a non-zero exit with an actionable message.
3. One page + one `MediaRecorder`: for each scene, start the gym scene via the director, play for `playMs`, record while capturing for `captureMs`; between scenes inject the page-side fade overlay (fade-to-black 250 ms, then fade-from-black 250 ms) so the recorder captures the transition.
4. Stop the recorder, run the existing probe (`isNonTrivialClip` / `evaluateAudioTrack` / `combineClipVerdict`), and write the single WebM to the configured output path (default under the gitignored `capture-output/` tree).
5. Emit the `--json` payload (per-scene timings + total duration + path); progress reporting reuses `formatProgress`.
6. Register `npm run capture:scenes` in `package.json`.

## Dependencies

- Pure config/planning module (sibling).
- Dev-gated director (sibling) for in-page scene switching.
- (Both of those depend on the test-first item.)

## Deliverables

- A working `npm run capture:scenes` producing one multi-scene WebM with fades plus the `--json` payload.

**discovered-from:AH-0MVF6Y29M005TEOG** (epic AH-0MVF3BESP005ZDAV).

## Problem

`node_modules/.vite` accumulates orphaned `deps_temp_<hash>` directories whenever a Vite dep optimisation is interrupted or collides — at intake there were 98 (141 MB), now **95 dirs / 158 MB total in `node_modules/.vite`**. They are pure cache debris: each is a partially written pre-bundle. The epic's AC3 timing work is unaffected functionally, but the debris wastes disk, slows directory scans, and is evidence that dep optimisation is re-running/colliding (which is one source of the transform/import variance measured in AH-0MVF6Y29M005TEOG).

## Why this was not fixed inline

`node_modules` is **shared by every worktree on this host via symlink**; deleting the cache while another agent's suite is mid-run can corrupt that run. The producer rule 'never destroy another agent's work' applies, so the cleanup needs a safe, quiescent mechanism rather than an opportunistic `rm -rf`.

## Expected change

A small, documented, safe cleanup path — e.g. `scripts/clean-vite-cache.mjs` that:
- refuses to run when any `vitest`/`vite` process is alive (or requires `--force`),
- removes only `deps_temp_*` (never the valid `deps/` bundle or `deps_ssr`),
- reports bytes reclaimed, and
- is documented in `docs/dev/test-suite-timing.md` (cache-hygiene section) and optionally wired into `scripts/hygiene_check.sh`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** A read-only `--dry-run` (default) reports the orphaned `deps_temp_*` count and bytes; `--apply` removes only those dirs and prints the reclaimed bytes.
- **AC2:** The script refuses to delete while a `vitest`/`vite` process is running unless `--force` is passed, and is covered by tests (dry-run classification, refusal path) that do not require a real cache.
- **AC3:** Documentation states why the cache is shared across worktrees and why the quiescence guard exists.
- **AC4:** After `--apply` on an idle host, `npx vitest run --project unit` still passes (cache regenerates cleanly).

## References

- AH-0MVF6Y29M005TEOG — measured the transform/import cost and rejected the optimizer/isolate/pool variants; notes the collision evidence.
- `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` — the existing periodic hygiene report this could extend.

# Align AI_Hell's test framework with the Tableau-Card-Engine game repos

AI_Hell runs a bespoke Vitest setup: `vitest.config.ts` + `vitest.projects.ts` with a
static classifier (`classifyTestFiles` / `isIntegrationTest` in `vitest.projects.ts`)
splitting test files into `unit` / `integration` projects, and test roots `src/`,
`scripts/`, `vite/` — there is **no top-level `tests/` directory**. Every sibling TCE
game repo (and the scaffold template `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`) uses the
standard layout: a `unit` project in `vite.config.ts` with
`include: ['tests/**/*.test.ts']` and no per-file classifier.

**Goal:** bring AI_Hell's test layout and project selection into line with the sibling
repos so cross-repo conventions, agent/audit tooling expectations (top-level `tests/`
tree), and the test skill's type profiles apply uniformly.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No test lost or doubled.** After migration, AI_Hell's full suite runs the
   identical set of `*.test.ts` files currently selected by
   `vitest.projects.ts::allTestFiles` (src/, scripts/, vite/) — same count and same
   per-file project membership; verified by a before/after selection diff.
2. **Standard layout adopted.** Tests live under a top-level `tests/` tree laid out to
   match sibling repos (e.g. `tests/deploy/` for infra guards, `tests/<area>/`),
   selected via the standard include globs in `vitest.config.ts` (or the config file's
   `test.projects`), with `tsconfig.json` including `tests/**/*.ts`.
3. **Isolation preserved.** Phaser/DOM-booting tests retain their separation from the
   fast node `unit` project (the deliberate unit/integration split — parent
   AH-0MVF3BESP005ZDAV, blocked child AH-0MVF6XV87001NSEJ). Alignment must NOT flatten
   Phaser-heavy tests into the node unit project or regress suite runtime. The
   `src/test/projectMembership.test.ts` guard is updated to assert the new layout and
   still passes.
4. **Tooling keeps working.** The test skill's per-type profiles
   (`.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json`, `.pi/test-config.json`) remain
   functional — update only if project names/commands change, and verify each type
   (`unit`, `coverage`, `e2e`) runs.
5. **Documentation updated.** Comments in the vitest config(s), AGENTS.md and any
   dev notes reflect the new layout. CHANGELOG.md excluded (ship skill).
6. **Full suite passes** with the changes.

## Constraints

- Refactor only — no change to app behaviour.
- Preserve the deterministic membership guard pattern (`vitest.projects.ts` is
  deliberately the single source of truth for selection; keep an equivalent guard).
- This item may also relocate `vite/viteWatchIgnore.test.ts` (added by the watch-ignore
  port, MS-0MVBEQ6MC004WRI0) into `tests/deploy/` for full parity — sequence after or
  alongside that port.

data.description:
# evaluate.mjs --tune: fail fast on unwritable --out and survive hard kill without dirty CSV

## Summary
During the 2026-10-21 end-to-end tune-loop verification (AH-0MVBNLM2V008XC8T), the negative-probe command

  node scripts/evaluate.mjs --tune --set enemy-configs.csv boss.health=7 --games 2 --ticks 200 --out /proc/nope/x

hung for 166.6 minutes inside a single Pi bash call before being killed (exit 137 / SIGKILL) — the largest
single tool call of the day (2.8 h of ~11.8 h active agent time). Instead of failing fast on the unwritable
output path, the CLI runs both sweeps first and validates the output directory only at write time. A hard
kill also means the in-memory CSV restore in the finally block cannot run: the session log shows the CSV
dirty (M src/data/enemy-configs.csv, changed md5) immediately after the kill (clean now, restored by later
session activity). Root cause to confirm during implementation; hypotheses: (a) output-dir validation
happens only after the sweeps, (b) no internal watchdog/timeout on the sweep, (c) SIGKILL (OOM/timeout)
skips the finally-based restore, (d) the pipe to tail can mask the true exit.

## User stories
- As a developer running tune-loop verification I want --tune to validate --out (and the CSV path) up-front
  so an invalid path fails in seconds, not hours.
- As a developer I want the tune/edit cycle crash-safe so even a hard kill never leaves the balance CSV
  edited in the worktree.

## Suggested approach
1. Validate options.outputDir and src/data/<tuneFile> before booting the SSR core or running any batch:
   a quick mkdir/writeability probe with a clear message and non-zero exit (ideally < 2 s).
2. Make edit/restore crash-safe: persist a small journal (target path + original bytes) beside the CSV
   before editing; restore/reconcile from the journal on next invocation (and document a manual repair
   path); do not rely solely on an in-memory finally.
3. Add a bounded-runtime watchdog or per-phase progress output for the sweep so an abnormal run cannot
   stall silently for hours; 2x200-tick games should take minutes, not hours.
4. Confirm the root cause with a repro before fixing (see hypotheses above); verify the observed exit code
   and CSV state in the repro.

## Acceptance criteria
1. The repro command above fails fast (< 2 s) with a clear "output directory not writable" diagnostic and
   a non-zero exit; demonstrated before and after the fix.
2. --tune with a valid --out still runs baseline -> edit -> re-run -> compare -> restore and exits 0;
   existing behaviour is preserved and existing evaluate/tune tests stay green.
3. A simulated hard kill (SIGKILL) at any point after the edit leaves the CSV byte-identical to the pre-run
   state, or a deterministic, documented repair path restores it exactly.
4. The full verification command used in AH-0MVBNLM2V008XC8T (including the negative probe) completes
   without hanging; the CLI help/docs mention the new validation.
5. Unit tests cover the writeability probe, the journal/restore under simulated kill, and the CLI exit
   codes; run under the project test policy (test skill).

## Context and references
- scripts/evaluate.mjs: main(), executeTune(), applyCsvEditFile(), restoreCsvFile()
- Related work items: AH-0MVBNITA0005VQGN (--tune CLI), AH-0MVBNISWE009QFBL (CSV edit guaranteed restore),
  AH-0MVBNLM2V008XC8T (end-to-end tune-loop verification, where this was observed)
- Observed in session 2026-10-21T12-15-12-077Z (finding #2 of the session-time analysis)
- discovered-from: analysis session of 2026-10-21
